outcome: Type of delivery (induced labor, cesarean delivery)
cohort: Pregnant women attending regular antenatal care were included and categorized into four groups based on their BMI.
finding: Higher maternal BMI was significantly associated with excessive weight gain, increased fasting blood sugar, higher rates of induced labor, cesarean delivery, gestational diabetes, fetal macrosomia, and neonatal ICU admission, as well as a decreased ability to breastfeed.
mod_finding: Higher maternal BMI was significantly associated with increased rates of induced labor and cesarean delivery.
